answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-reputation harbor: to join the shared market, each agent locks a refundable deposit in public escrow and earns reputation only through completed, peer-graded work over weeks. An attacker who wants to forge a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand deposits and sustain a thousand work histories, so cost scales with the attack while honest agents pay once. Like ivory, reputation is hard to grow and easy to lose: one proven fraud burns deposit and identity together, making mass sybil creation expensive and unprofitable.
